elements.label: Table 4.15
elements.title: Steps for Calculating the Correlation Coefficient
elements.details:
| Step | Representation in Symbols |
|-------|---------------------------|
| 1. Calculate the sum of the x-values. | Σx |
| 2. Calculate the sum of the y-values. | Σy |
| 3. Multiply each x-value by the corresponding y-value and calculate the sum of these xy products. | Σxy |
| 4. Square each x-value and then calculate the sum of these squared values. | Σx² |
| 5. Square each y-value and then calculate the sum of these squared values. | Σy² |
| 6. Determine the value of n, which is the number of data pairs. | n |
| 7. Use these results to then substitute into the formula for the correlation coefficient. | r = (nΣxy - (Σx)(Σy)) / sqrt[(nΣx² - (Σx)²)(nΣy² - (Σy)²)] |
elements.summary: This table outlines the step-by-step process and symbolic representation for calculating the Pearson correlation coefficient from paired data values.
